top_comments.author: @esuvii
top_comments.text:
A compiler is a deterministic tool that given the same setup will always transpile into the same low level instructions. It's a method of abstraction from the hardware level to tools that humans can more easily use to solve complex problems.

This is not at all comparable to using an LLM, which translates plain text into code based on a statistical model, and given the same set of inputs will not always give the same output.

I usually agree with Linus on most takes but he is just saying buzz-phrases here that don't have any substance. AI can be a useful tool when used responsibly, but it is nothing like a compiler.

top_comments.author: @shaneorourke110
top_comments.text:
It’s not the same issue at all. Compilers take precise instructions from the original code and turn it into machine code or whatever. The AI will make assumptions, will fix bugs before they exist, can decide architecture, run tests, can create novel solutions that the user didn’t directly ask for. 
When AI creates 99% of code, it’s like a department director or CEO saying “I wrote 99% of this code” (when it was the devs writing it). Providing natural language instructions to create huge codebases (not to mention testing, root cause analysis, bug fixes etc) is not the same as writing the same code manually line by line.

That said, AI is here now, and in the hands of developers it really does make writing code easy. It still takes a developer’s guidance to create something special.

I’m not bashing AI and “vibe coding”, I’m just saying that the analogy is wrong
